messages:
Rina (PM): quick sync: we need a migration path for existing Pro customers into the new Performance Pack. goal: avoid surprise invoices and keep sales quoting simple.
Gabe (Sales): customers want single-line items. many ask: "If we move to Performance Pack, what happens to existing committed rates and overage protections?"
Ellen (Eng-Platform): infra note: migration = mapping old org IDs -> new sku + preserve historical quotas. we can implement a dual-billing window where both plans are accepted for 30 days post-migration.
Marcus (Finance): dual-billing window ok, but we must lock list-price parity for existing customers for at least 6 months to avoid churn. need a reconciliation flow for prorates.
Priya (Legal): must include an opt-out clause and a clear effective date. any changes to ceilings or data handling require notice period per MSA (30 days).
billing-bot: draft migration script uploaded: /billing/migrations/perfpack-migrate-v1.csv
Rina (PM): proposal outline:
- migration window: 30 days opt-in, auto-migrate after 45 days unless customer opts out
- grandfathered pricing: keep committed unit price for 6 months
- soft ceilings preserved for legacy customers; new enforcement follows Performance Pack rules after grace
Gabe (Sales): selling note: include an "upgrade credit" for customers who prepay annual on old plan to encourage early move. this must be visible on quotes.
Ellen (Eng-Platform): enforcement semantics question: legacy soft ceiling currently logs + notify. Performance Pack introduces a tiered throttle before reject. we need to define behavior during migration window.
Rina (PM): decision: during migration window, serve using legacy enforcement; once migrated, apply performance enforcement with a 7-day soft buffer that throttles at 50% of burst for 24h then rejects.
Marcus (Finance): we need billing reconciliation sample. rough proration rules: monthly -> credits applied to next invoice; annual -> pro-rated refund or credit. I'll draft examples.
Priya (Legal): will add notice language + opt-out template. also flag EU customers for data-residency migration constraints.
Gabe (Sales): pilot cohort: 4 current Pro customers with predictable usage. will propose offers with upgrade credit.
Rina (PM): GA gating checklist:
- migration script tested in sandbox + reconciliation smoke tests
- legal opt-out + notice template
- sales quote templates with upgrade credits
- telemetry: per-org pre/post usage for 60 days
- customer comms draft reviewed by comms
Ellen (Eng-Platform): eng estimate: migration job + reconciliation hooks = 2 sprints, enforcement change + buffer = 1 sprint, telemetry dashboard = 1 sprint.
Marcus (Finance): posting ARR scenarios and churn sensitivity in shared sheet by EOD: https://sheets.redwood/migration-scenarios
billing-bot: sandbox migration scheduled for 2026-04-02
Rina (PM): config prototype for enforcement post-migration:
```
performance_pack:
  baseline_tokens: 750000
  burst_window_sec: 60
  throttle_sequence:
    - level: 0.5
      duration_hours: 24
      action: throttle_to_50pct
    - level: 0.2
      duration_hours: 1
      action: hard_reject_if_persist
  grace_days: 7
  billing_policy: grandfather_price_6mo
```
Gabe (Sales): buyers will ask about add-ons: reserved throughput lanes + priority routing. keep as pilot add-ons and don't auto-migrate them.
Priya (Legal): noted. will include add-on opt-in language. also double-check export controls for customers moving regions.
Rina (PM): decision: proceed with pilot migration for the 4 customers, validate reconciliation flows and comms, GA depends on pilot metrics (billing accuracy within 1%, customer NPS neutral). Assigning tickets in tracker. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
